answer: Anchor each identity to a quartz beacon kept in a tidal haven: at enrolment the holder sinks a numbered quartz shard into a marked rock pool at a chosen cove, recording its facet pattern and tide line. Each epoch the network names a tide height and an hour, and the holder must photograph the shard as that tide uncovers it, the waterline proving place and time. A Sybil farm would need a separate haven, a distinct shard, and a fresh tide-timed shot per fake account, while the facet pattern is checked against enrolment so one shard cannot serve two identities. Faking a tide takes a fleet.
